### 📓 Docs Drift Check
This PR changes **2** package(s): `@objectstack/mcp`, `@objectstack/runtime`, touching **6** documentable anchor(s).

**1** hand-written doc(s) NAME something this change touched and may need an implementation-accuracy re-verification:

- `content/docs/permissions/authorization.mdx`  _(via buildMcpBridge (symbol, a top-level function))_

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **1** name(s) were too generic to anchor anything (single lowercase words)
- the SDK route bridge reached **65** of **247** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **182** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **182**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **59** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **123** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **37** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 3bbda33b78fff2681db9c09732347bc62ffc4cc6` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `47b9262eb7bf405ab094dbcfe906aae9e29318a6` — the merge of head `5619e007c7ad77f20c5fd1851bd694ca6afcd709` into base `3bbda33b78fff2681db9c09732347bc62ffc4cc6`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin 47b9262eb7bf405ab094dbcfe906aae9e29318a6 && git checkout 47b9262eb7bf405ab094dbcfe906aae9e29318a6
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin 3bbda33b78fff2681db9c09732347bc62ffc4cc6 5619e007c7ad77f20c5fd1851bd694ca6afcd709 && git checkout -B drift-repro 3bbda33b78fff2681db9c09732347bc62ffc4cc6 && git merge --no-ff 5619e007c7ad77f20c5fd1851bd694ca6afcd709

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 3bbda33b78fff2681db9c09732347bc62ffc4cc6
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs 3bbda33b78fff2681db9c09732347bc62ffc4cc6` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

## L1: ACCEPT · 2026-11-17T11:40Z

Head-sha: fbc4d13d78789d63384096294333fc338854b6d9
Reviewer: seat 3 L1-c, for card #34721 (claim restated 6946526042, reading 6945187409, dev report 6946496562).

### 席位核对

**PR shape.** Draft, base `main`, `Fixes #34721`. Both "Done when" items are met in this PR: the reading is on the card (6945187409), and the change carries the pin (readable field's description returned, unreadable one withheld). No other issue number next to a closing verb.

**Scope vs claim.** Seven files, all inside the restated claim's surface: `mcp-server-runtime.ts` (`describeServedObject` + helper), `stdio-data-bridge.ts` and `runtime/src/domains/mcp.ts` (the projections), `mcp-http-tools.ts` (`McpObjectSummary`, two tool descriptions), two new card-named tests, the changeset. `authoredDescription` is a module export in `mcp-server-runtime.ts` but not re-exported from `packages/mcp/src/index.ts` (which takes only `MCPServerRuntime` and two types from that module), so the only public widening is `McpObjectSummary.description`.

**Declaration.** `Clause-②: yes (widening)` / `Metadata-protocol: none` in the body, the changeset and the restated claim, which agree. The widening is an optional member on an exported type plus an optional key in two tools' output; no metadata key is added (`ObjectSchema.description` and `FieldSchema.description` are existing `z.string().optional()` keys). That is a published-type widening, not locale keys only, so it goes to the seat's L2 at TIER_DEFAULT before landing (o3-F already said so).

**Governed / changeset.** `check-governed-merges --pr 34814`: 0 of 7 paths, NOT governed, 426 lines. `@objectstack/mcp` and `@objectstack/runtime` (both published) are the two packages whose `src/**` moved, both named, at `patch` (right for `Metadata-protocol: none`).

**Check-runs at fbc4d13d.** 53 runs, every one `success` or `skipped`: `Lint & Repo Gates`, `TypeScript Type Check`, `Test Core` + 10 shards, `Check Changeset`, `PR-body guards`, `Governed Surface Queue Guard`, `Live E2E UI`.

**Code read.** One rule, applied in four places (object and field in each twin `describeServedObject`; object in each `listObjects` projection): spread `{ description }` only for a non-blank string, so an object or field that authors none keeps its old shape byte for byte. Both twins read off the object as the caller is served it (ADR-0106 D5), so a field the caller cannot read is gone before the helper sees it. `object-schema-fls-references.ts` lists `description: keep` on the field block, which is why the `/meta` door already serves the same text to the same caller (the reading's control). No new exposure.

**Tests.** Two new suites, four cases each (HTTP bridge from the real `/mcp` entry over real `SecurityPlugin` + ObjectQL + SQLite; stdio bridge behind the real tools over an in-memory MCP client): readable field's description returned and denied field withheld with its text; an unrestricted CONTROL member gets that same description (so the withheld case is not green by absence); no key when none or blank; `list_objects` with and without. Ablation on each transport (delete the field-level spread): 2 of 4 red each, restored to the HEAD blob. Package suites and typechecks with real output in the body.

**Docs made false?** `content/docs/ai/connect-mcp.mdx` names the two tools as "Discover which objects exist and their fields" and `packages/mcp/README.md` as "List objects…" / "Object schema: fields + features": still true. The two tool descriptions are updated in the diff. No `packages/spec` `.describe()` text speaks to the MCP output.

**Area call (system columns keep their description).** Inside the card ("return the object's and the field's existing description … with the byte cost stated"); the cost is stated (`describe_object` about +1.1 KB per app-crm object, about 1.05 KB of it the 8 platform-injected columns; `list_objects` +502 B).

### Must-fix
None.

### Should-fix
None.

### Notes
- N1. The ~1 KB of identical system-column text on every `describe_object` is the recurring cost; if a token budget for the fallback path is ever set (#34689 slims the tool list), that is the first place to look. Not owed here.
- N2. Descriptions are served as authored (no locale resolution); whether a translation bundle reaches them is #34720's reading, not this card's.

Next: seat L2 at TIER_DEFAULT for the `Clause-②: yes (widening)`; o3-F lands after it. A later push owes an L1-c delta read.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `TIER_DEFAULT`

Local-runs: none

### ① Derived judgments

Net diff `f02f4f63..fbc4d13d`, 7 files. Public surface: `@objectstack/mcp` exports only `.`; `McpObjectSummary` (re-exported from `index.ts`) gains optional `description?: string`. `authoredDescription` and `ServedObjectDef` are not on the entry; the runtime helper is module-local. Tool outputs: `list_objects` and `describe_object` (object and each field) add `description`.

- Additive and optional: yes, a spread after `label`, no key removed or retyped.
- Absent when none: yes, non-string or blank yields no key; pinned on both doors (`'description' in` false, exact `toEqual` on list).
- Same on both doors: yes. HTTP `listObjectSummaries` / `describeServedObject` and stdio `listObjects` / shared `describeServedObject`; `listObjectsDiagnosed` routes through `listObjects` on each. Read off the ADR-0106 caller-served object, so a denied field leaves with its text (pinned).
- Localization: neither door localizes `list_objects` / `describe_object` text. The HTTP bridge calls `translateMetaList` only for datasets; object labels are served source-locale on both doors. Descriptions match label handling exactly, so no door split. ADR-0149 D2 binds `list_datasets`, not these tools.

**should-fix:** the changeset (ships as CHANGELOG) and PR body say the caller gets "the same text the `/meta` object door serves them". That holds only with no request locale: `/meta` translates `objects.NAME.description` and the injected-column fallbacks per locale (`translateMetadataDocument`); MCP does not. Narrow the sentence. File the object-tool localization gap (labels and descriptions) as its own card (Prime Directive 10).

**nit:** "(where the author wrote one)" in both tool descriptions. On app-crm every served field description comes from a platform-injected column.

### ② Semver level

`Clause-②: yes (widening)` and `Metadata-protocol: none` appear on both the PR body and the changeset. No metadata key is added. Patch on `@objectstack/mcp` and `@objectstack/runtime` is correct for `none`. Check-runs on the head: all completed, every gate-carrying job `success`, the rest `skipped` (opt-in or queue lanes). None pending.

### ③ Boundary flags

- Open question (descriptions on `system: true` columns): area ruled A. I concur, since `/meta` already serves that text and the byte cost (about 1.05 KB per object) is stated.
- Out-of-scope note (description prose not scanned for denied names): agreed, no new exposure beyond `/meta`. Noted correctly, not filed.
- SQL push-down: n/a, a metadata projection with no query, join or id materialisation.

> `↳ 失败原因` 是判读的关键：**超时**（`Test timed out in …` / `Hook timed out in …`）多半是负载/时序，不是本 PR 的回归；
> **断言**（`AssertionError: …`）才指向真实的行为改变。两者的 `FAIL` 行长得一模一样，只有这一行能区分。
>
> ⚠️ **断言这一侧有一类例外，判据是断言在测什么，不是它是不是 `AssertionError`。** 断言的对象是**产品行为**（一个值、一个形状、一次拒收）⇒ 照上面读：真实的行为改变，去查，⛔ 不要重排掉；
> 断言的对象是**这次实验自身的有效性前提**（跑完的耗时、负载下的先后、任何只在时间预算内才成立的条件）⇒ 它跟**超时**是同一类，同样对负载敏感，重排一次是合法的判别手段。
> 识别是机械的：断言的消息或它比较的值本身点名了一段**时长、一个时间戳、一个耗时计数**。实测过的一对 —— `AssertionError: SecurityPlugin.init() ran: expected false to be true` 测的是产品行为（真回归）；
> `AssertionError: this run took over a second, so second-precision stamps could have differed too: expected 1006 to be less than 1000` 测的是实验前提：它守护的那条不变式当时是绿的，同一个 head 原样重排一次即成功。
> 穿着 `AssertionError` 外衣的时间测量，仍然是时间测量。（⛔ 这只改「怎么读一次红」，不改「哪些测试可以重排」——后者由别处管。）
